chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of the two عليهمَا ٱلسَّلَامُ, he said:
I asked him about the nights in which ghusl (ritual bath) is recommended in the month of Ramadan, so he said: “The nineteenth night, the twenty-first night, and the twenty-third night.”

And he said: “The twenty-third night is the night of al-Juhanī, and his report is that he said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘My dwelling is far from al-Madīnah, so designate for me a night in which I may come in.’ So he instructed him regarding the twenty-third night.”

key_terms.رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ: the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of fasting in which these nights occur
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ ثَلَاثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ: the twenty-third night of Ramadan, singled out for special merit
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ ٱلْجُهَنِيِّ: the designation associated with the twenty-third night in this report
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath recommended on certain nights of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Which nights of Ramadan is ghusl recommended, and what is the significance of the twenty-third night?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ghusl (ritual bath) is recommended on the nineteenth, twenty-first, and twenty-third nights of Ramadan. It also highlights the special distinction of the twenty-third night through the report of al-Juhanī, whom the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله directed to that night due to its significance.
